title: English Confession 1647: saving faith and assurance of being in grace are distinct
source_text: XXXVI. Sed praeterea huic sententiae aperte favet Confessio Anglicana anni 1647. nam separatis capitibus agit de Fide salutari, & de certitudine quam quis habet quod sit in Dei gratia, supponens haec esse inter se diversa. Et capite 18. ubi agit de ista certitudine, dicit eam non ita esse de essentia fidei, quin vere fidelis possit eadem carere, & eam expectare, & luctari cum multis difficultatibus, priusquam certitudinis ejus particeps fiat.
pass_a_gloss: But besides, the English Confession of the year 1647 openly favors this opinion; for in separate chapters it treats of saving Faith, and of the certainty which someone has that he is in God's grace, supposing these to be diverse from each other. And in chapter 18, where it treats of that certainty, it says it is not so of the essence of faith that a truly faithful person cannot lack it, and await it, and struggle with many difficulties, before he becomes partaker of that certainty.
pass_b_english: English Confession (1647) separates saving faith from certainty of being in grace.
Ch. 18: that certainty is not so of faith’s essence that a true believer cannot lack it.
He may await it and struggle with many difficulties before sharing in it.
